title: Priv VPC IAM access matrix + minimal-priv Terraform module and upgrade safety
creator: Marcus Nguyen
description: Create a reusable Terraform module and supporting automation that emits a least-privilege RBAC surface for Private (VPC) deployments. The module should: produce an access matrix (human-readable CSV/JSON), generate IAM roles and policies using param-driven patterns, include safeguards for safe in-place upgrades, and wire health-check hooks for runtime role-boundary validation. This ticket covers design, implementation, tests, docs, and a phased rollout plan for existing private customers.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module (registry-style) that can be consumed by private deployment stacks and parameterized for account/role boundaries
Module outputs an access matrix (CSV and JSON) listing principals, intended permissions, and justification tags
Least-privilege policies are generated as policy documents (not inline strings) and pass our policy linter with no failures
Upgrade plan that performs non-disruptive role rotation and policy diffs via canary accounts/workloads
Automated health-check Lambda/kube-checker that validates role assumption and permission subsets daily
Integration tests covering cross-account assume-role flows, permission-deny scenarios, and drift detection
Documentation in Confluence + example Terraform usage pattern in the priv-deploy repo
Security sign-off obtained and module published to internal module registry

implementation_notes: Module composition: main module produces iam_roles (map), policy_documents (file objects), outputs: access_matrix_s3_path, role_names, policy_arns
Policy generation: templated JSON using vars.grants -> compile into aws_iam_policy_document, then aws_iam_policy resource. Avoid inline policies on compute resources where possible.
Upgrade safety: implement 'safe_apply' helper that calculates policy diff, creates new policy with temp suffix, updates role to assume new policy, validates health checks, then deletes old policy

Health checks: Lambda in customer account triggered by EventBridge daily; it will assume each role and run minimal assertions (ListBuckets for S3-role, Encrypt/Decrypt for KMS-role) and report to CloudWatch metrics + SNS for failures.
Testing: unit tests with localstack for IAM policy generation; integration tests run in isolated staging AWS accounts; canary rollout uses 3 non-prod customer accounts before production.
Docs & examples: include terraform root module example with 'role_binding' pattern, migration guide for older inline policies, and a checklist for safety gates before upgrades.
risks: Existing customer stacks with hard-coded inline policies may fail upgrade without manual intervention
Cross-account assume-role latencies in some regions could cause health-check flakiness — need retry/backoff and regional test coverage
KMS key scoping errors could result in data access regressions if not explicitly configured
Policy explosion: many tiny policies may increase management surface; we should group by logical service where appropriate
